question.text: A light-emitting diode (LED) has a voltage drop of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> across it and passes a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mA</mi></math>. When it operates with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> battery through a limiting resistor <math><mi>R</mi></math>, what is the value of <math><mi>R </mi></math>(in ohm)?

solution.text:
Current in the circuit = 10 mA = 10×10-3 A

and voltage in the circuit = 6-2= 4 V

from Ohm's law,

V=IR

∴ R=VI=410×10-3= 400 Ω
